title: 2015 HMMT November Guts Problem 35
statement: Let \(n\) be the smallest positive integer such that any positive integer can be expressed as the sum of \(n\) integer 2015th powers. Find \(n\). If your answer is \(a\), your score will be \(\max \left(20-\frac{1}{5}\left|\log _{10} \frac{a}{n}\right|, 0\right)\), rounded up.

solutions.text:
Answer:
\(2^{2015}+\left\lfloor\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{2015}\right\rfloor-2\)

In general, if \(k \leq 471600000\), then any integer can be expressed as the sum of \(2^{k}+\left\lfloor\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^{k}\right\rfloor-2\) integer \(k\) th powers. This bound is optimal.
The problem asking for the minimum number of \(k\)-th powers needed to add to any positive integer is called Waring's problem.
